messages.content:
You write original English listening practice texts for Taiwanese students (high school or university). Each text is read aloud by text-to-speech, then the student types each sentence from dictation and repeats it aloud.
Write natural, spoken English with correct standard spelling. Give the text a short English title.
Return the text as lines: one sentence per line for a monologue; for a dialogue, one speaker's turn per line, alternating between two people, with no speaker names or labels.
Keep each sentence about 5 to 25 words. Write numbers, times, and amounts the way they are usually written (9:30, $15, 20%).
Do not write about real people, real brands, or real current events; invent names and details. Keep it appropriate for students.
Match the requested level, length (in words), and format. If a topic or keywords are given (in any language), build the text around them.
Also give titleZh, the title in Traditional Chinese (Taiwan usage), and subtitle, one Traditional Chinese sentence of at most 30 characters saying what the listener will hear.
In any Chinese text, write digits and Latin letters half-width (4號月台), never full-width.
{"topic":"","scenario":"a manager explaining a change in the work schedule","level":"CEFR B2 to C1: natural, varied vocabulary and sentence structure","words":200,"format":"monologue"}

message.content: {"title":"Schedule Update for the Team","titleZh":"團隊排班調整說明","subtitle":"聽一位經理說明工作時間調整細節。","lines":["Good morning everyone, I have a few important updates about our work schedule.","Starting next Monday, we will adopt a staggered start time to reduce peak congestion in the office.","Most team members will begin between 8:00 and 9:30, depending on their role and daily tasks.","Please check the new rota on the shared drive to see your assigned start time.","We know this change may affect commute plans, so we asked the HR team to coordinate with local transit options.","Each person will still work their full contracted hours, and lunch breaks remain unchanged.","On Wednesdays only, the office will close at 3:00 for team briefings and training sessions.","If you cannot attend a Wednesday session, notify your manager in advance so we can arrange a make-up or provide materials.","Overtime will be paid or taken as time off in line with existing company policy.","We are introducing one floating work-from-home day per week for eligible staff to improve flexibility.","Eligibility details and the application process are explained in the memo attached to the rota.","Please note that critical client meetings will require in-person attendance regardless of your floating day.","Team leaders will revise project timelines to reflect the new schedule and ensure deliverables remain on track.","If a scheduling conflict arises, discuss alternatives with your supervisor as early as possible.","We will review the impact of these changes after eight weeks and welcome your feedback.","Send any questions or concerns to the scheduling inbox so we can address them efficiently.","Thank you for your cooperation as we try to create a more balanced and productive work environment.","I appreciate your patience while we implement these adjustments and ensure a smooth transition."]}
